question.text: What will be the 2-party Gallagher disproportionality index for North Carolina's House races in 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the 2-party Gallagher disproportionality index calculated from the results of the 2026 U.S. House of Representatives [elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_North_Carolina) in North Carolina. The value will be calculated by subtracting the GOP percentage of the merged Republican and Democratic vote for the U.S. House of Representatives across all NC congressional districts from the GOP percentage of congressional seats won, then taking the absolute value of that number.

research:
I could not find anything that settles this yet. The election is on 2026-11-03, so no vote totals exist. The answer depends mostly on two things: how many of the 14 seats Republicans win, and the GOP share of the combined R+D vote.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-29: The Wikipedia page named in the question has no results yet. It lists Republican and Democratic nominees in all 14 districts, so none of the races is uncontested between the two parties. The general election is 2026-11-03. [Wikipedia 2026 NC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_North_Carolina)
- How the calculation works: each Republican seat is worth 7.14 points of seat share. 11 GOP seats is 78.57%, 10 is 71.43%, 9 is 64.29% and 8 is 57.14%. The index is the absolute gap between that seat share and the GOP percentage of the combined R+D vote.

## 2. Current status
- 2025: The GOP legislature redrew the map mid-decade, aiming for an 11-3 Republican delegation. They changed District 1 (Democrat Don Davis) and District 3, and NC-1 moved to about R+8 according to Inside Elections. [The Nation](https://www.thenation.com/), [ABC11](https://abc11.com/post/1st-congressional-rematch-most-watched-us-house-races/19730542/)
- Ratings and polls, seat by seat:
  - **NC-1:** Toss-up at Cook (Oct 9) and Inside Elections (Oct 15), Lean D at Sabato (Oct 20). The latest poll, RedBox (D), Oct 20-23, has Davis 45%, Buckhout 44%.
  - **NC-3:** Likely R at Cook (Oct 23). A Tulchin (D) poll from July-August had Murphy 44%, Smith 41%.
  - **NC-11:** Toss-up at Cook and Sabato.
  - **NC-7 and NC-9:** Two Democratic-sponsored polls each showed the Republican up by about 4-6 points (Rouzer 49-43 head-to-head in August; Hudson 46-42 in October).
  - **Other districts:** NC-5, 6, 8 and 10 are Solid R and NC-2, 4 and 12 are Solid D. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_North_Carolina), [NC Newsline](https://ncnewsline.com/2026/10/19/a-tale-of-two-farmers-ager-balkcom-compete-for-nc-11-seat/?channel=brytalocals)
- Statewide generic ballot: ECU, Sept 29-Oct 2, had Democrats 50%, Republicans 46%. Co/efficient (R), Oct 6-8, had R 46%, D 45%, but the Wikipedia page lists it under NC-1 and may not be statewide. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_North_Carolina)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-29: Early voting passed 2.1 million ballots, up 36% from the same point in 2022. Unverified detail from the news-API summary: Democrats still hold a plurality of early voters. [CBS17](https://www.cbs17.com/news/your-local-election-hq/nc-early-voting-numbers-top-2-million-a-large-increase-from-2022-midterms/)
- 2026-10-29: NC-1 is the most expensive House race on record, with $52.9M in ads according to AdImpact. [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6181205-nc-house-race-record-spending/)
- 2026-10-28: A national Fox News poll has Democrats ahead 54-45 on the generic ballot. [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/opinion/lee-carter-america-angry-everyone-who-will-actually-vote)
- 2026-10-27: Democrats were nearly 41% of early voters. [WLOS](https://wlos.com/news/local/north-carolina-early-voting-turnout-2026-midterm-election-ballots-buncombe-county)
- 2026-08-10: Rep. Chuck Edwards (NC-11) dropped out after a House Ethics report. State Rep. Jennifer Balkcom replaced him as the GOP nominee against Jamie Ager. [NC Newsline](https://ncnewsline.com/2026/08/10/ncgop-to-select-new-nc-11-candidate-after-us-rep-edwards-withdrawal/)

## 4. Base rates
- 2024: R 2,889,657 votes, D 2,328,248, so R had 55.38% of the two-party vote. Republicans won 10 of 14 seats (71.43%). **Index about 16.0.** [Wikipedia 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_North_Carolina)
- 2022, under a court-drawn map: R 1,956,906, D 1,795,170, so R had 52.15%. Seats split 7-7 (50%). **Index about 2.2.** [Wikipedia 2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_North_Carolina)
- Earlier years, from memory and not checked:
  - 2020: 8 of 13 seats R with about 50% of the vote, index about 11-12.
  - 2018: 10 of 13 seats R with about 51% of the vote, index about 25.
  - 2016: 10 of 13 seats R with about 53% of the vote, index about 24.
- Pattern: under GOP-drawn maps the index has run about 16-26. Under the 2022 court map it was about 2.
- Illustrative 2026 combinations:
  - 11 R seats at 50% R vote: about 28.6.
  - 10 R seats at 49%: about 22.4.
  - 9 R seats at 49%: about 15.3.
  - 9 R seats at 47%: about 17.3.
  - 8 R seats at 48%: about 9.1.
- In a Democratic-leaning year, more D votes push the index up when seats hold, but each lost GOP seat pulls it down by 7.14 points.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi, Democratic NC House seats (as of 2026-10-29): 3 at 3%, 4 at 10%, 5 at 41%, 6 at 19%, 7 at 11%, "Above 7" at 20%. The "Above 7" price looks odd given the map and is probably illiquid.
- Polymarket, same question: 4 at 11.5%, 5 at 44%, 6+ at 39%.
- Kalshi, other markets:
  - NC-3: Murphy winning by 1+ points at 52%, which suggests roughly 50/50 odds of a Democratic upset.
  - NC-9: Hudson at 50%+ of the vote, 65%.
  - NC-10: Harrigan winning by 10+, 60%.
  - NC-12: Alma Adams at 76%+ of the vote, 65%.
  - Control of the US House: Democrats at 91%.
- Polymarket, NC-6: McDowell (R) favored. The 12-15 point margin bucket is at 40%, but the 6-9 bucket is close behind at 33%.
- I found no published expert forecast of the Gallagher index itself.

## 6. Upcoming events
- 2026-11-03: Election Day. The key seats are NC-1, NC-11 and NC-3, plus the margins in NC-7 and NC-9.
- Mid-November: Counties finish canvassing and the State Board of Elections certifies results, which is when final vote totals are set. Any close race could go to a recount.
- Also matters: turnout in safe Democratic seats (NC-12, 4, 2) inflates the Democratic statewide vote share without changing seats.

Nothing has been decided yet: Election Day is 2026-11-03. Using the past results below, the 2-party index for North Carolina was 11.8 in 2020, 2.2 in 2022 and 16.1 in 2024. Markets expect Democrats to win about 5 of the 14 seats. If so, the index would be about 13 to 17 for a statewide Republican vote share of 47 to 51%.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-29: The [Wikipedia 2026 NC House page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_North_Carolina) has no results yet. It shows 14 seats, a pre-election split of 10 R and 4 D, and Election Day as 2026-11-03. Official totals will come from the NC State Board of Elections; county canvass and state certification usually finish in late November.
- How the number is calculated: with 14 seats, the Republican seat share can be 78.57% (11 R), 71.43% (10), 64.29% (9), 57.14% (8) or 50% (7). The index is the absolute gap between that share and the Republican share of the combined R+D vote. Third-party votes are left out.

### 2. Current status
- 2026-10-29: Nothing is settled. Voting ends 2026-11-03.
- Every district I could check (NC-1 to NC-11 and NC-13) has both a D and an R candidate. I did not confirm NC-12 or NC-14. Kalshi's NC-12 market (Alma Adams) suggests that race is contested.
- The map is the 2025 mid-decade redraw. It changed NC-1 and NC-3 to aim for an 11-3 Republican delegation. [The Nation](https://www.thenation.com/)

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-29: More than 2.1 million early ballots have been cast, 36% more than at this point in 2022. Democrats are the largest group, at about 41% of early voters. [CBS17](https://www.cbs17.com/news/your-local-election-hq/nc-early-voting-numbers-top-2-million-a-large-increase-from-2022-midterms/), [WLOS](https://wlos.com/news/local/north-carolina-early-voting-turnout-2026-midterm-election-ballots-buncombe-county)
- 2026-10-29: NC-1 (Don Davis, D, vs. Laurie Buckhout, R) is the most expensive House race on record, with $52.9M in ads. [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6181205-nc-house-race-record-spending/)
- 2026-10-20: NC-1 polls are tied or close: RedBox (D) has Davis 45, Buckhout 44; co/efficient (R) has Buckhout 43, Davis 42. Cook and Inside Elections rate it Tossup; Sabato rates it Lean D. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_North_Carolina)
- 2026-10-19/20: In NC-9, a PPP (D) poll has Hudson (R) 46, Ojeda (D) 42. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_North_Carolina)
- 2026-10-02: The DCCC added NC-13 (Brad Knott, R) to its target list. Cook still rates it Solid R. [NC Newsline](https://ncnewsline.com/2026/10/02/national-dems-expand-us-house-battlefield-targeting-knott-in-nc-13/)
- Statewide generic-ballot polls: ECU (Sep 29 to Oct 2) has D 50, R 46. Catawba/YouGov (September) has D 47, R 38. NYT/Siena (June) has D 49, R 44. Nationally, Fox News has D 54, R 45. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_North_Carolina), [Fox](https://www.foxnews.com/opinion/lee-carter-america-angry-everyone-who-will-actually-vote)
- August 2026: In NC-11, Chuck Edwards withdrew after an ethics recommendation, and Jennifer Balkcom (R) replaced him. Democrat Jamie Ager was described as the favorite, with the GOP at about 32% in markets in August. Trump won the district by about 10 points in 2024. [PredictionHunt](https://www.predictionhunt.com/news/balkcom-replaces-edwards-in-nc-11-gop-climbs-aug-21-2026), [WLOS](https://wlos.com/news/local/republican-congressional-nominee-balkcom-begins-84-day-campaign-for-nc-11-seat-congressman-chuck-edwards-house-ethics-fairness-womens-sports-act-jamie-ager-democrat)
- NC-3 (Murphy, R): Cook rates it Likely R. A Tulchin (D) poll from July/August had Murphy 44, Smith 41.

### 4. Base rates (my calculations from Wikipedia totals)
- 2024: R 2,889,657 votes, D 2,328,248. R share of the 2-party vote 55.38%; R seat share 71.43% (10 of 14). **Index 16.05.** [Wiki 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_North_Carolina)
- 2022: R 1,956,906, D 1,795,170. R 2-party share 52.16%; seats 50% (7 of 14). **Index 2.16.** [Wiki 2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_North_Carolina)
- 2020: R 2,631,336, D 2,660,535. R 2-party share 49.72%; seats 61.54% (8 of 13). **Index 11.82.** [Wiki 2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_North_Carolina)
- The index changes a lot from one cycle to the next (2 to 16), mostly because of court-ordered and legislative map changes.
- Illustrative 2026 cases:
  - D wins 5 (R 64.29%) with R at 47 to 51% of the vote: index about 13 to 17.
  - D wins 6 (R 57.14%): about 6 to 10.
  - D wins 4 (R 71.43%) with R at about 50 to 52%: about 19 to 21.
  - D wins 3: about 26 to 29.
  - D wins 7: about 0 to 2, which is below the question's 5 to 30 range.

### 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi, Democratic seats won in NC (2026-10-29): 3 at 3%, 4 at 10%, 5 at 41%, 6 at 19%, 7 at 11%, "Above 7" at 20%. Those prices look inconsistent; "Above 7" may overlap with other buckets.
- Polymarket, same question: <3 at 1.75%, 3 at 3.3%, 4 at 11.5%, 5 at 44%, 6+ at 39%.
- Polymarket NC-3 margin: Republican-win buckets add up to about 47%. Kalshi has Murphy winning by 1+ points at 0.52.
- Kalshi NC-9: Hudson getting at least 50% at 0.65. NC-10: Harrigan winning by 7+ at 0.75. NC-12: Adams getting at least 74% at 0.83. Polymarket NC-6: R margin of 12 to 15 points at 0.405.
- Kalshi House control: Democrats 0.91.
- I found no expert or market forecast of the Gallagher index itself.

### 6. Upcoming events
- 2026-11-03: Election Day. NC-1, NC-11, NC-3, NC-13 and NC-9 decide the seat count.
- Mid to late November: provisional ballots, county canvass and possible recounts in close races. North Carolina allows a recount when the margin is 1% or less.
- Around 2026-11-24: state certification, before the question resolves around 2026-12-01.
- Statewide turnout, including the early-vote surge, mainly moves the vote-share part of the index. One more or one fewer seat moves the index by about 7.1 points.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** The election is on 2026-11-03, 5 days away. Final certified totals arrive in mid-to-late November, and the question resolves around 2026-12-01.

(b) **Latest known value:** The latest is from 2024, with an index of about 16.0 (10 of 14 seats R, 55.4% R two-party vote). In 2022, under the court-drawn map, it was about 2.2. No 2026 results exist yet.

(c) **If nothing changed:** If the current market favorite happens (9 R seats, 5 D) with an R two-party share near 48-49%, the index is about 15-16.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** The trend is a Democratic-leaning environment, with the national generic ballot at D+6 to D+9 and NC polling around D+2 to D+4.
- If the wave sweeps NC-1, NC-11 and NC-3, Republicans hold 8 seats. The R vote would be about 47%, giving an index of about 10.
- If one more seat (NC-7 or NC-9) also flips, the index falls to about 2-4.

(e) **Historical variation:**
- Each seat moves the index by 7.14 points. The vote share typically varies by about 2 points around expectation.
